html:
The underground railway of Moscow, opened on 15 May 1935. It is famous for its grand stations and is one of the busiest metros in the world.

The first line ran about eleven kilometres. Stalin's government made it a showpiece of socialism, a palace for the people. Stations were built with marble, mosaics, chandeliers, bronze statues and murals celebrating workers, soldiers and Soviet history. Komsomolskaya and Mayakovskaya are among the best known. Young communists and other workers dug much of it by hand.

Many stations lie deep underground. In the Second World War they served as bomb shelters, and Stalin gave a speech in Mayakovskaya station in November 1941 as the Germans neared the city.

The system kept growing through the Soviet years and after, and a large new circle line was finished in 2023. It came seventy years after the first metro, the London Underground of 1863, and its palace stations were meant to show that socialism could outbuild the capitalist cities.
